prompt: What three things does a role assignment join?

choices.text: A user, a password and a resource
choices.why: No password is involved: signing in is Entra ID's business, and access is decided after it.

choices.text: A resource, its owner and a list of the people allowed to use it
choices.why: Azure keeps no list of people on a resource; it collects assignments at every scope above it.

choices.text: A principal, a role and a scope
choices.why: Right. Who, which list of operations, and which box.

choices.text: A tenant, a subscription and a region
choices.why: A region plays no part in access, and a tenant is where principals live, not a piece of the assignment.

prompt: Contributor's `actions` is `*`. Which line of its `notActions` keeps it from giving anybody access?

choices.text: `Microsoft.Subscription/cancel/action`
choices.why: That stops it cancelling the subscription; access is elsewhere.

choices.text: `Microsoft.Authorization/*/Write`
choices.why: Right. Role assignments are under `Microsoft.Authorization`.

choices.text: `Microsoft.Compute/galleries/share/action`
choices.why: Sharing an image gallery is one of the removed operations, but it is not role assignment.

choices.text: `Microsoft.Blueprint/blueprintAssignments/write`
choices.why: A blueprint assignment is a different resource, from a retired service.

prompt: Match each built-in role to what it allows.
hint: One of them gives access and does nothing else.
right_distractors: reading the blobs in every storage account

prompt: Why can a Bicep file name the Reader role by the id `acdd72a7-3385-48ef-bd42-f606fba81ae7` in any company's tenant?

choices.text: A built-in role's id is one and the same GUID in every tenant on the planet
choices.why: Right. That is why the role is named by id rather than by display name.

choices.text: Because each tenant copies Reader under that id when it is created
choices.why: Nothing is copied: the definition is Microsoft's, assignable everywhere.

choices.text: Because Bicep translates the id into the local name
choices.why: Bicep passes the id through unchanged, as the compiled template showed.

choices.text: It cannot: each tenant gives Reader an id of its own
choices.why: The built-in ids are fixed. Custom roles are the ones whose ids differ.

prompt: Reading a blob's contents is listed in a role's `___`, separate from the management operations.
hint: Its counterpart for management is called `actions`.

prompt: What does `notActions` do in a role definition?

choices.text: It denies the operations to the person, whatever other roles they hold
choices.why: That is a deny assignment. A not-action removes from its own role only.

choices.text: It lists operations that need approval first
choices.why: Approval is a feature of lesson 10's elevation, not of a role definition.

choices.text: It records operations the role used to have
choices.why: It is not history; it is a live subtraction.

choices.text: It takes operations out of what that role's actions allow
choices.why: Right. Actions minus not-actions, inside one role.

prompt: `bia` holds Contributor on `shop-prod` and User Access Administrator on `rg-shop-prod`. May `bia` create a role assignment in `rg-shop-prod`?

choices.text: No: Contributor's notActions forbid it everywhere below the subscription
choices.why: A not-action only narrows Contributor; it does not cancel another role.

choices.text: No: the narrower scope loses to the wider one
choices.why: Scopes do not compete. Every assignment that covers the resource counts.

choices.text: Yes, through the second role, since roles add up
choices.why: Right. Effective permissions are the sum of the assignments.

choices.text: Only after the subscription's Owner approves
choices.why: Nothing waits for approval here: the two assignments simply add up.

prompt: `can.py` answered `no` for Owner reading a blob with `--data`. What does that show?

choices.text: That the storage account has public access switched off
choices.why: No account was asked. The answer came from the role definitions alone.

choices.text: That `can.py` has a defect, since Owner may do everything
choices.why: The program applied the documented rule: Owner's actions are `*`, its dataActions empty.

choices.text: That blobs are protected by a deny assignment
choices.why: No deny assignment was involved; the program does not even read them.

choices.text: Owner's `*` covers management only; its data list is empty
choices.why: Right. Data operations need a role whose `dataActions` names them.

prompt: A security review says: "Only Storage Blob Data Reader can read the order exports, because Contributor has no dataActions." What is missing from the sentence?

choices.text: Contributor lists the keys, and a key opens every blob
choices.why: Right. `listKeys` is a management action, and the key bypasses roles.

choices.text: That Reader also has dataActions `*/read`
choices.why: Reader's `*/read` is in `actions`, not `dataActions`.

choices.text: That deny assignments block Contributor from storage
choices.why: No such deny assignment exists by default.

choices.text: Nothing: the data plane is fully separate from management
choices.why: Only while the shared keys are switched off.

prompt: Put Resource Manager's steps in judging a request in the order Microsoft documents.
hint: What can refuse before anything else is read?
items: check the deny assignments that cover the resource
gather the role assignments of the principal and its groups
look for the operation in those roles, actions minus not-actions
evaluate the conditions on the assignment
trap: The deny assignments come first: one that applies refuses the request and nothing else is read.

prompt: Who creates a deny assignment?

choices.text: Any Owner, to protect a resource group
choices.why: An Owner cannot create one directly, which is part of why it can bind an Owner.

choices.text: Azure, for features such as deployment stacks
choices.why: Right. A deployment stack with deny settings and a managed application each place one.

choices.text: User Access Administrators, as the opposite of an assignment
choices.why: They create role assignments; deny assignments are not theirs to make.

choices.text: Nobody now: they were removed with Blueprints
choices.why: They exist today; deployment stacks create them.

prompt: How many role assignments may one subscription hold, by the limit Microsoft says it will not raise?
hint: The same number as custom roles per tenant.

prompt: Reader is assigned to a group at the subscription `shop-prod`. Where can its members read?

choices.text: In `shop-prod` and in the management group above it
choices.why: An assignment never reaches up.

choices.text: Everywhere inside `shop-prod`, groups and resources
choices.why: Right. Every group and every resource in it, and nothing beside it.

choices.text: In every subscription of the tenant
choices.why: Only an assignment on the root management group would do that.

choices.text: Only in resource groups created after the assignment
choices.why: Inheritance covers what exists and what is added later alike.

prompt: Why does the lesson give the assignment the name `guid(resourceGroup().id, groupId, readerId)`?
hint: What happens on the second deployment?

choices.text: To hide which group was given the role
choices.why: The group is in the properties for anybody who can read the assignment.

choices.text: Because Bicep refuses any other kind of name for a role assignment at compile time
choices.why: The compiler accepts any name; it is Resource Manager that wants a GUID.

choices.text: So a redeploy lands on the same assignment
choices.why: Right. The same three inputs give the same GUID every time.

choices.text: To make the name random, so two assignments never collide
choices.why: `guid()` is deterministic, which is the whole point.

prompt: The custom role `Shop App Restarter` lists `assignableScopes: [subscription().id]`. What does that decide?
hint: Where may the role be handed out?

choices.text: Which resources the role's actions apply to
choices.why: The assignment's scope decides that; this list decides where assignments may be made.

choices.text: Who may restart the web app
choices.why: Who is decided by assignments, not by the definition.

choices.text: The region the definition is stored in
choices.why: Role definitions are stored globally, not by region.

choices.text: Where it may be assigned
choices.why: Right. Here, inside this subscription only.

prompt: Which of these are habits the lesson recommends? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Assign roles to groups rather than to people
choices.why: Right. Membership changes; assignments stay.

choices.text: Give Contributor on the subscription so nobody is blocked
choices.why: That makes every mistake as large as possible.

choices.text: Assign at the smallest scope that works
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Prefer a specific role to a general one
choices.why: Right. Network Contributor over Contributor, for a network.

choices.text: Make custom roles assignable at `/` so they can be reused
choices.why: A role assignable everywhere is one more thing everybody can grant.

prompt: Bicep's `___()` function hashes its arguments into the same identifier every time, which is how the lesson names role definitions and assignments.
The on-call developers must restart the shop's web app and nothing else, in `rg-shop-prod` only. Which arrangement does the lesson lead to?
hint: A narrow role, a group, a small scope.

choices.text: `Shop App Restarter` for the on-call group on `rg-shop-prod`
choices.why: Right. A specific role, given to a group, at the smallest scope.

choices.text: Owner for the on-call group on `rg-shop-prod`, removed after each incident
choices.why: Owner can also grant access; and removing by hand after each night is what lesson 10 replaces.

choices.text: Contributor for each developer on `shop-prod`
choices.why: Too wide in role, in scope and in the people named one by one.

choices.text: Reader on `rg-shop-prod`, since restarting is a read
choices.why: `restart/action` is not a read, and `*/read` does not match it.

prompt: Which question can `can.py` answer?
hint: It reads role definitions and nothing else.

choices.text: Whether `bia` may delete `vnet-shop-prod` today
choices.why: That needs `bia`'s assignments, groups and any deny assignment: Resource Manager's facts.

choices.text: Whether a condition on an assignment holds for a blob
choices.why: Conditions are step 4, which the model leaves out.

choices.text: Which roles are assigned at `rg-shop-prod`
choices.why: Assignments live in Resource Manager; the program has never seen one.

choices.text: Whether the lists of the roles it is given allow an operation
choices.why: Right. Step 3 of the documented order, on the roles you give it.
